name: batch-11
prompt:
Create ONE production game-icon SPRITE ATLAS, exactly 3 columns by 3 rows on a square canvas, ideally 2048x2048, genuinely TRANSPARENT alpha PNG. Input image is the user's approved style sheet, STYLE reference only. Match that soft tactile dimensional 3D collectible family: gentle warm upper-left diffuse studio light, rounded yet faithful forms, bright pastel/candy color, subtle ambient occlusion, restrained material detail. Each object's true material remains recognizable: paper, wood, glass, metal, woven cloth. No same-clay treatment on everything. No heavy dark outlines or flat vector art.

CRITICAL PACKAGING: There are EXACTLY NINE equal square virtual cells in a regular 3x3 grid. Draw ONE specified object/group centered within EACH virtual cell, at ONLY 48–52% of cell width/height, with at least 24% EMPTY TRANSPARENT MARGIN ON EVERY SIDE. Nothing may touch a virtual cell edge or cross into a neighbor. All strings, handles, leaves and shadows stay inside their own cell. Think SMALL MINIATURE ICONS with LARGE EMPTY GUTTERS, NOT large illustrations filling the sheet. Icon centers are x=16.67%,50%,83.33%, y=16.67%,50%,83.33% of the image. Each icon must fit in a box 18% of the overall image size. Empty space between shapes is essential. No visible grid lines, no backgrounds, no color squares, no borders, no captions, numbers, words, ID labels, titles or decorative props. Empty padding is genuine alpha transparency, NOT a drawn checkerboard. Top-left through bottom-right order is mandatory; do not swap cells. Each tile will be cropped at exact one-third boundaries into a separate icon. Keep centered and similarly weighted, readable at 32–66px. All objects fully in frame, no cropping. Only allow inscription glyphs explicitly specified in subject. Do not invent sacred symbols, cultural ornament, claims or text. No extra humans/hands/landscape/pedestals. Subject list in strict row-major order:
1. Cell row 1, column 1: A tapered warm-brown wooden churn barrel with two dark grey metal hoops, a fitted wooden lid and one vertical plunger rising through its center. The plunger has a short dark-brown grip; do not turn it into a crank mechanism.
2. Cell row 1, column 2: A round warm-wood frame drum with a pale cream hide head, a muted green inner rim and a short diagonal double-ended wooden beater. Keep the shallow circular frame and two darker rounded beater ends.
3. Cell row 1, column 3: A square warm-brown wooden hand coffee grinder with a front drawer and small green knob, a shallow brass-colored metal hopper above, and a bent grey steel crank ending in a green grip. Keep the hopper, crank and drawer as separate recognizable parts.
4. Cell row 2, column 1: An open red-orange paper umbrella with one cream wedge, visible radial bamboo ribs, a straight brown shaft and a short muted-green handle. Preserve the faceted paper canopy and pointed central apex; no printed motifs.
5. Cell row 2, column 2: Two pairs of warm-brown hollow wooden castanet shells, each pair slightly open, joined at the top by dark teal cord loops. Keep the rounded teardrop shell forms and visible light inner edges; no hands or extra decoration.
6. Cell row 2, column 3: A pale olive bamboo tipping tube on two short darker bamboo supports, poised above a shallow turquoise pool with a grey stone rim. Water falls from its open right end and a small knocking stone sits at the left; keep the central pivot readable.
7. Cell row 3, column 1: A flat painted wooden pull-string puppet with a cream round head, orange hat, teal torso and blue jointed arms and legs. One thin tan cord and a small wooden bead hang below the body; preserve the visibly separate hinged limbs.
8. Cell row 3, column 2: A compact asymmetrical trapezoid-shaped honey-colored wooden zither with five parallel silver-grey strings, a dark pin bar at the right and a small round sound hole near its lower edge. Keep exactly five visible strings and the sloping left side.
9. Cell row 3, column 3: A natural honey-brown wooden swing with two A-frame end supports, one heavy top beam and a broad plank seat suspended by two rigid wooden arms. Small grey pivot pins connect the arms to the beam; use no chain or rope suspension.
